scope: Imported-island all-eight local expedition, CPU BFS over actual visible geometry, real keyboard walking and repair inputs, typed explanations, finale, supported Save and Continue reload. No wallet interaction, seeded state, teleport or injected completion.

repairs.rationale: The 3-unit weight at one metre and 2-unit weight at one and a half metres balance the six-unit load. I anchor the rope and retain the pulley guard, trading lift speed for controlled cargo handling. I protect shoreline nests, keep access clear and inspect the rope before lifting.

Inlet four supplies twelve units. The relief bypass releases two while outlet three delivers six, leaving pressure four. I retain the intake screen and relief rather than forcing more pressure. This protects clean reedbed drainage and keeps valves accessible for safe isolation and maintenance.

The bank shield prevents erosion. Nursery stop three retains three units while the open creek takes five. I keep both branches connected and store the obstruction in its onsite rack, balancing habitat water with drainage and keeping inspection access clear.

Opposing diagonals provide eight units of rated load capacity through both bank shoes and the joined deck. I tension the handrail and avoid new bed supports, preserving creek flow instead of obstructing habitat for extra support. The shoes and brace joints remain accessible for inspection.

The twenty-four tooth driver and twelve tooth driven gear turn the sixty-rpm shaft into one hundred twenty rpm. I connect the coupling and guard and use the bluff service pad. This balances output with safe isolation, avoids nesting habitat and leaves maintenance access clear.

The twelve-volt source, one-amp fuse and regulator feed the six-watt lamp through its protected return. I turn the shade down and retain the sleeved route, trading woodland glare for useful path light while preserving fuse isolation and maintenance access.

Six units of supply pass through the filter. The village gets four and habitat two along descending branches within capacity. I keep the overflow and filtration, balancing village supply with habitat flow and leaving filter and valve maintenance accessible.

The protected twelve-volt circuit supplies the clear lens on the safe plinth. The reflector points into the coastal sector and the shield excludes inland nesting glare. I preserve fuse isolation and clear maintenance access, choosing controlled signal coverage instead of unnecessary wider light.
